title: Equilibrium non-existence in generalized games
summary_en: When does a strategic-form game fail to admit a Nash equilibrium? Tóbiás studies generalised games — games where each player's feasible action set depends on others' actions — and identifies the topological conditions on action correspondences under which non-existence of equilibrium becomes generic. The paper extends the standard Glicksberg / Reny existence results and provides counter-examples showing the limits of the existence-theorem toolkit.
data_used: Theoretical paper in game theory. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Foundational theoretical input for any policy analysis that relies on Nash-equilibrium predictions in environments with constrained-strategy interactions — coalition-formation games, capacity-constrained auctions, network-formation games used in industrial-policy modelling. The paper's non-existence results warn against blind application of equilibrium-existence results in models with action-dependent feasible sets.
